([[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]]) | college = [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] (1997–2001) | draft_year = 2001 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 44 | draft_team = [[Chicago Bulls]] | career_start=2002 | career_end=2009 | career_number = 21 | career_position = [[Small forward]] | years1 = 2002 | team1 = [[Saskatchewan Hawks]] | years2 = 2002 | team2 = [[Red Bull Thunder]] | years3 = {{nbay|2002|full=yes}} | team3 = [[Miami Heat]] | years4 = 2003 | team4 = [[Dakota Wizards]] | years5 = {{nbay|2003|start}} | team5 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years6 = 2004 | team6 = [[Makedonikos B.C.|Makedonikos]] | years7 = 2004–2005 | team7 = Dakota Wizards | years8 = 2005–2006 | team8 = [[Barangay Ginebra Kings]] | years9 = 2006 | team9 = [[Artland Dragons]] | years10 = 2007 | team10 = [[CB Axarquía|Clinicas Rincón Axarquía]] | years11 = 2007–2008 | team11 = [[Melbourne Tigers]] | years12 = 2008–2009 | team12 = [[El Jaish SC (basketball)|Al Jaysh Army SC Doha]] | highlights = * [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]] All-Rookie Team (2002) * [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-10 Player of the Year]] ([[2000–01 Pacific-10 Conference men's basketball season|2001]]) * 2× First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] (2000, 2001) }} '''Sean Lampley''' (born September 3, 1979) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. ==College career== Lampley played at the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California]], leading the Golden Bears to victory over [[Clemson University|Clemson]] in the 1999 [[National Invitational Tournament]] and earning MVP honors. In 2001, he led the team to the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]], but the Bears lost in the first round to [[Fresno State University|Fresno State]]. Lampley ended his career as the only player in school history to rank in the top 10 in points (1,776, 1st), rebounds (889, 4th) and assists (295, 10th). He was named Pac-10 Player of the Year and Honorable Mention All-America his senior year by the AP.[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/sean_lampley/bio.html Sean Lampley NBA.com Bio] Lampley's career scoring record stood until he was surpassed by point guard [[Jerome Randle]] on March 13, 2010, with 1,790 career points.{{cite web|title=California beats UCLA 85–72 in Pac-10 semifinals|date=March 13, 2010|access-date=March 15, 2010|publisher=[[Pac-10]].org|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recap?gid=201003120095}} ==Professional career== Lampley was selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the 2nd round (44th pick) of the [[2001 NBA draft]]. He began his career with the [[Saskatchewan Hawks]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) and earned All-Rookie Team honors in 2002.{{cite web |title=Sean Lampley minor league basketball statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-lamplsea001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=June 27, 2021}} Although he never wore a Bulls uniform, Lampley played 35 games for the [[Miami Heat]] during the 2002–03 season and 10 games for the [[Golden State Warriors]] during the 2003–04 season. He competed with the [[Sacramento Kings]] in 2006 summer league play. Lampley only played a total of 45 games in his NBA career with career averages of 4.5 points and 2.1 rebounds. His final NBA game was played on December 12, 2003, in an 85–96 loss to the New Orleans Hornets where he recorded 9 points and 2 rebounds. ===Oceania career=== Lampley signed with the [[Melbourne Tigers]] of [[Australia]]'s [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] in December 2007.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=73468 |title=Muursepp cut by Tigers |access-date=December 30, 2007 |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303223618/http://www.nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=73468 |url-status=dead }} After arriving in the country only 2 days prior, Lampley made his debut in the NBL's biggest attendance of the season, scoring 10 points (on 3/5 shooting) and pulling down 4 rebounds in the Tigers' victory over the [[South Dragons]] at [[Melbourne Arena]] on December 15. He played with the Oaks Card Club squad in 2006–2007.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=73494 |title=Dragons v Tigers 12/15/2007 – boxscores |access-date=December 30, 2007 |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303191945/http://www.nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=73494 |url-status=dead }} His signing filled the void left by recently de-listed player [[Martin Müürsepp|Martin Muursepp]],[http://www.news.com.au/heraldsun/story/0,21985,22995393-11088,00.html Tigers go all out to retain Sean Lampley] who suffered from poor form partly due to an ongoing battle with an ankle injury.
